question: When part of a tree is not the part that actually got shown - it was superseded and replaced by a stand-in while it was still settling - the per-node enter and leave notifications for the superseded part still run, because the code that decides which nodes entered and which left compares only the old set against the new set. It has no notion of where the shown region stops, so nodes below that boundary are treated exactly like nodes the user is really looking at: their callbacks fire for a region that was never presented, and they fire against membership that was published without any record of which branch it belonged to, so an observer re-entering during publication sees the wrong extent. The concept that would fix this does not exist anywhere in the repository yet - there is no name to search for. Elsewhere in the folder the same hazard is handled on purpose: one library carries an explicit flag down the tree so that a subtree currently held back does not run its attach and detach work, another attaches and detaches only along the branch that is genuinely depended upon, and another funnels all observer notification through a single batching point so that membership and notification cannot interleave. Which files decide entered-and-left membership without a boundary, and which own the scoped-notification contract they have to be brought in line with?

anchor.pr_title: fix(router-core): skip lifecycle callbacks below fallback boundaries

grader_notes.why_cross_repo: ANCHOR (real bug, TanStack/router PR #8165 'skip lifecycle callbacks below fallback boundaries', merged 2026-09-06 as 2f20c00224c5 - AFTER the pinned commit 3dee5b2e9453, so the pin is the buggy parent and the fix postdates the May 2026 cutoff). At the pin `runRouteLifecycle(router, previous, matches, owner?)` (packages/router-core/src/router.ts:931-936) decides entered/left membership purely by comparing the previous match set against the new one; it has no parameter describing where the rendered region stops, so onEnter/onLeave fire for matches below a fallback boundary that were never presented. commitMatches (load-client.ts) publishes membership with no record of which branch it belongs to, so an observer that synchronously re-enters during publishMatches sees the wrong extent. The fix introduces lifecycleEnd() and threads previousEnd/nextEnd through commitMatches, hydrate and the server loader. The citations own the scoped-notification contract correctly: React carries offscreenSubtreeIsHidden down the commit walk so a subtree held back behind a fallback does not run its layout effects (ReactFiberCommitWork.js, with the visibility model in ReactFiberOffscreenComponent.js); jotai mounts and unmounts only along the branch actually depended upon (src/vanilla/internals.ts mountAtom/unmountAtom/mountDependencies); query funnels every observer notification through one batching point so membership and notification cannot interleave (notifyManager.ts).
